sourceHtml:
When you deploy an agent to production, one of the hardest questions is whether it’s actually working? The bar isn’t whether it runs. It’s whether it does what the business needs, at scale. Many teams will tell you they can’t really see this. They spot-check outputs, watch latency, and collect user feedback when they can get it. None of that tells you whether the agent finished the user’s task, stayed on topic across a long session, leaked personally identifiable information (PII), or quietly skipped half the steps it was supposed to follow.

Figure 1: Teams usually watch surface signals, but business outcomes are decided by the agent behaviors below the waterline

Agent evaluation solves this problem. What makes this challenging is that a good score on one metric can hide a failure on another. A support agent can resolve every ticket and still expose personal information in its replies. In this case, the agent is failing although it has a high completion rate. To get evaluation right, measure the behaviors that matter for each agent, at the right level of detail.

This post shows how to do this on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. We use the AgentCore built-in evaluators together with the DeepEval and AutoEval evaluators directly from AgentCore Evaluations.

Start with business outcomes, instead of metric names

The most common mistake is to start with the metric list and pick the names that sound right. “Helpfulness sounds good, so we use it.” The result runs and produces numbers, but it gives almost no useful insight. The metric fits its label, not what success means for the agent.

Instead, start with three steps.

  1. Define success in business terms. For a customer support agent, that might be first-contact resolution. For a research agent, it might be producing a complete, well-sourced answer grounded entirely in retrieved documents. For a content moderation assistant, it means flagging everything that should be flagged and only what should be flagged.
  2. Break the outcome into observable behaviors. A customer support agent that achieves first-contact resolution will typically complete the user’s stated goal, stay coherent across turns when the issue requires clarification, keep responses within compliance boundaries, and correctly invoke backend tools like ticket creation or order lookup.
  3. Map each behavior to an evaluator at the right level. Trace-level metrics cover per-turn or per-tool-call behaviors. Session-level metrics cover outcomes that only make sense when you look at the whole conversation.

Figure 2: Translating a business outcome into observable behaviors and then into specific evaluators at the trace or session level

This three-step process is the mental model that makes evaluation useful. The rest of this post is about what AgentCore gives you to execute it.

The evaluator catalog

AgentCore has a broad catalog of evaluators from three sources:

  1. Built-in evaluators are authored and quality-tested by AWS. You reference them by their ID (Builtin.GoalSuccessRate, Builtin.Helpfulness, and 13 more) and the service handles everything else. They are benchmarked for reliability and cover the common dimensions, so they are the straightforward place to start.
  2. Third-party managed evaluators come from DeepEval and AutoEval, two established open-source evaluation libraries. When you use them in managed mode, AgentCore hosts the code, picks the judge model, and runs inference on its own capacity, exactly like built-in evaluators. If your team already uses one of these libraries in development, you can run the same metrics in production without a separate evaluation service.
  3. Custom evaluators take a built-in or third-party evaluator as a base, so you can swap in your own model and modify the prompt or rubric.

Figure 3: The three evaluator tiers trade AWS quality assurance for increasing control over the model and account that run inference

After creation, a custom derived evaluator is used exactly like other ones.

The evaluator landscape

AgentCore ships with a broad catalog of evaluators, so you rarely start from a blank page. Before you write a custom judge, check whether one already measures the behavior you care about. The following figure shows the whole landscape.

Figure 4: The full evaluator landscape on AgentCore across built-in, DeepEval, AutoEval, and custom sources

Built-in AWS evaluators fall into five groups:

  1. Response quality covers whether the answer is accurate, grounded, and well-formed: Correctness, Faithfulness, Helpfulness, ResponseRelevance, Conciseness, Coherence, InstructionFollowing, and Refusal.
  2. Task and goal completion has GoalSuccessRate, which looks at the whole session and asks whether the user’s goal was met.
  3. Tool use has ToolSelectionAccuracy and ToolParameterAccuracy, which check whether the agent picked the right tool and passed it the right arguments.
  4. Skills has SkillSelectionAccuracy and SkillInstructionFollowing, for agents that load skills: was the right skill invoked, and were its steps followed?
  5. Safety has Harmfulness and Stereotyping.

Next to these are three ground-truth trajectory checks: TrajectoryExactOrderMatch, TrajectoryInOrderMatch, and TrajectoryAnyOrderMatch. They compare the agent’s actual tool path against the one you expected. Reach for them when how the agent got there matters as much as what it produced.

DeepEval provides managed open-source metrics in four groups:

  1. Task and goal completion: TaskCompletion, GoalAccuracy, and ConversationCompleteness.
  2. Conversational quality: TurnRelevancy, KnowledgeRetention, and Summarization.
  3. Tool use: ToolUse.
  4. Safety: Bias, Toxicity, and PIILeakage.

These metrics are especially useful for multi-turn agents. ConversationCompleteness catches an agent that answers the latest message but quietly drops earlier requests. KnowledgeRetention catches an agent that forgets something the user said three turns ago.

AutoEval offers more specialized signals:

  1. Security flags malicious output, such as attempts to inject instructions or reveal system prompts.
  2. Possible catches over-cautious agents that wrongly declare a valid task impossible.
  3. Humor matters for consumer-facing agents where personality is part of the product.

Custom evaluators. When no evaluator in the catalog fits, you can write a custom LLM-as-a-judge.

Every evaluator’s exact definition, scoring scale, and input requirements are in the prompt template library in the AgentCore documentation. That includes the judge prompt it uses, the trace or session level it runs at, and whether it needs a reference answer or an expected trajectory. You can call the ListEvaluators API to get the full catalog and your own custom evaluators in one response.

Multi-dimension evaluators

Each evaluator so far returns one score per trace or session. That works when you measure one behavior. But step 2 of the outcome mapping rarely gives one behavior per evaluator. A support reply must resolve the issue, follow refund and data policy, and stay professional. One judge that weighs all three returns one number, and you cannot tell which criterion drove it.

A multi-dimension evaluator is a custom LLM-as-a-judge with a list of dimensions instead of one scale. Each dimension has its own name, instruction, and numeric or categorical scale. The judge reads the trace once and scores every dimension in the same call. AgentCore returns one result per dimension.

Figure 5: A multi-dimension evaluator scores several dimensions from a single judge call and returns one result per dimension with no composite score

Use a multi-dimension evaluator when your success criteria can fail independently, such as an answer that’s accurate but non-compliant, or resolved but rude. It also needs every criterion to be judgeable from the same evidence, so that one judge call replaces several near-identical evaluators re-reading the same trace. When you score the criteria separately, you can gate on each one. A release that improves tone but regresses policy compliance fails, and a single blended score would hide that.

Keep criteria in separate evaluators when an established built-in or third-party metric already covers them, such as Builtin.Correctness or ThirdParty.DeepEval.PIILeakage. Also keep them separate when they need different levels or judge models, because the dimensions in one evaluator share a single level and model. Do the same when some criteria need ground truth such as {expected_response} or {assertions}. Keeping the reference-free criteria in their own evaluator means it can still run on live traffic.

Example stacks by agent type

Each of the following stacks starts with two or three evaluators that best match the business outcome. Add the others when you find a failure mode the first set misses. Evaluators marked “needs ground truth” run in batch evaluation only, because live traffic has no reference answer or expected path.

Customer support Multi-step research Domain content (medical, legal, financial)
Business outcome Problem solved in one session, with no downstream risk Complete, well-sourced answer through a defined workflow Correct, unbiased, secure answers within the domain
Main risk Dropped requests, unsafe or non-compliant replies Right answer through the wrong tool path, or lost context in long sessions A wrong answer. A wrong answer is worse than no answer.
Start with

Builtin.GoalSuccessRate (anchor)

ThirdParty.DeepEval.ConversationCompleteness

ThirdParty.DeepEval.PIILeakage

Builtin.TrajectoryAnyOrderMatch (needs ground truth)

ThirdParty.DeepEval.GoalAccuracy

ThirdParty.DeepEval.KnowledgeRetention

Builtin.Correctness (needs ground truth)

ThirdParty.DeepEval.PIILeakage

ThirdParty.AutoEval.Security
Add when needed

ThirdParty.DeepEval.Toxicity

ThirdParty.AutoEval.Security (sensitive account data)

Builtin.Helpfulness

Builtin.SkillInstructionFollowing

ThirdParty.AutoEval.Possible

ThirdParty.DeepEval.Bias

Builtin.Helpfulness
Derived evaluators Optional Use for trajectory and skill metrics if inference must stay in your account Almost always, so every judge call stays under your data governance

Running evaluations: The three modes

AgentCore supports three evaluation modes.

On-demand evaluation is the fastest feedback loop. Pass a session directly to client.evaluate() during development or debugging. Every evaluator in the system, including third-party, works here.

import boto3

client = boto3.client('bedrock-agentcore')

response = client.evaluate(
    evaluatorId="ThirdParty.DeepEval.TaskCompletion",
    evaluationInput={"sessionSpans": session_span_logs}
)

for result in response["evaluationResults"]:
    print(f"Value: {result.get('value')}")
    print(f"Explanation: {result.get('explanation', '')}")

Online evaluation attaches to your live agent runtime and samples real traffic at a configured rate. This is your production health signal. Built-in and third-party evaluators mix freely in a single online evaluation config.

Batch evaluation runs a defined evaluator stack against a fixed set of sessions: your golden dataset for regression testing before releases. Use this to confirm that a prompt change or model upgrade preserved quality across every dimension you care about.

All three modes use the same evaluator IDs. Switching from on-demand development testing to production online evaluation is a configuration change, not a code rewrite.

Putting it together

Increasingly, the hard part is choosing which evaluators to pick. Pick the two or three behaviors that best show whether you reached your business outcome, and measure those first. Add an evaluator when you find a failure your current set missed.

To see the full catalog, call the ListEvaluators API. It returns the built-in, DeepEval, and AutoEval evaluators in one response along with any custom evaluators in your account. Before you pick any of them, answer two questions: “What does success look like for this agent?” and “What behavior in the trace shows that it happened?”

About the authors

translation.html:
将智能体部署到生产环境时，最难回答的问题之一是，它真的发挥作用了吗？衡量标准在于它能否大规模地满足业务需求。许多团队会告诉你，他们实际上看不清这一点。他们抽查输出、监测延迟，并在能获取用户反馈时收集反馈。但这些都无法告诉你，智能体是否完成了用户的任务，是否在长时间会话中始终围绕主题，是否泄露了个人身份信息（PII），或者是否悄悄跳过了本应遵循的一半步骤。

图 1　团队通常关注表面信号，但业务结果取决于水面之下的智能体行为

智能体评估解决了这一问题。难点在于，一项指标的高分可能掩盖另一项指标上的失败。客服智能体可能解决了所有工单，却仍在回复中泄露个人信息。在这种情况下，尽管完成率很高，智能体仍然是不合格的。要做好评估，就要以恰当的细致程度，衡量对每个智能体而言重要的行为。

本文介绍如何在 Amazon Bedrock AgentCore 上实现这一点。我们直接通过 AgentCore Evaluations 使用 AgentCore 内置评估器，以及 DeepEval 和 AutoEval 评估器。

从业务结果出发选择指标

最常见的错误是先看指标列表，再挑选听起来合适的名称。“有帮助性听起来不错，那就用它。”这样做能运行并生成数字，却几乎无法提供有用的洞察。指标符合它的名称，却没有体现智能体取得成功的含义。

可以从以下三个步骤入手。

  1. 用业务语言定义成功。对于客服智能体，成功可能意味着首次联系即解决问题。对于研究智能体，成功可能意味着给出完整、来源充分且完全以检索到的文档为依据的答案。对于内容审核助手，成功意味着标记所有应当标记的内容，并且只标记这些内容。
  2. 将结果拆解为可观察的行为。能够在首次联系时解决问题的客服智能体，通常会完成用户明确提出的目标，在需要澄清问题时保持多轮对话连贯，使回复保持在合规边界内，并正确调用创建工单或查询订单等后端工具。
  3. 将每种行为映射到恰当层级的评估器。追踪记录级指标涵盖每轮对话或每次工具调用中的行为。会话级指标涵盖只有查看完整对话才有意义的结果。

图 2　将业务结果转化为可观察的行为，再转化为追踪记录级或会话级的具体评估器

这三个步骤构成了让评估发挥作用的思维模型。本文其余部分将介绍 AgentCore 提供了哪些能力来落实这一流程。

评估器目录

AgentCore 提供了丰富的评估器，来自三个来源。

  1. 内置评估器由 AWS 编写并进行质量测试。你通过 ID（Builtin.GoalSuccessRate、Builtin.Helpfulness 及另外 13 个）引用它们，其余工作由服务处理。它们经过可靠性基准测试，并覆盖常见维度，因此是便捷的入门选择。
  2. 第三方托管评估器来自 DeepEval 和 AutoEval，这两个成熟的开源评估库。在托管模式下使用它们时，AgentCore 会托管代码、选择裁判模型，并使用自身的计算资源运行推理，方式与内置评估器完全相同。如果你的团队在开发中已经使用其中一个库，就可以在生产环境中运行相同的指标，无需单独部署评估服务。
  3. 自定义评估器以内置或第三方评估器为基础，允许你换用自己的模型，并修改提示词或评分标准。

图 3　三类评估器在 AWS 质量保障与对推理所用模型和账户的控制权之间有所取舍，控制权逐级增加

创建后，自定义派生评估器的使用方式与其他评估器完全相同。

评估器全景

AgentCore 自带丰富的评估器，因此你很少需要从零开始。在编写自定义裁判之前，先检查是否已有评估器能够衡量你关心的行为。下图展示了完整全景。

图 4　AgentCore 的完整评估器全景，涵盖内置、DeepEval、AutoEval 和自定义来源

AWS 内置评估器分为五组。

  1. 回复质量涵盖答案是否准确、有据可依且形式规范，包括 Correctness、Faithfulness、Helpfulness、ResponseRelevance、Conciseness、Coherence、InstructionFollowing 和 Refusal。
  2. 任务与目标完成情况包含 GoalSuccessRate，它会查看整个会话，判断用户目标是否达成。
  3. 工具使用包含 ToolSelectionAccuracy 和 ToolParameterAccuracy，用于检查智能体是否选择了正确的工具，并传入了正确的参数。
  4. 技能包含 SkillSelectionAccuracy 和 SkillInstructionFollowing，面向会加载技能的智能体，检查是否调用了正确的技能，以及是否遵循了技能步骤。
  5. 安全性包含 Harmfulness 和 Stereotyping。

此外，还有三种基于基准真值的执行轨迹检查，分别是 TrajectoryExactOrderMatch、TrajectoryInOrderMatch 和 TrajectoryAnyOrderMatch。它们将智能体实际采用的工具调用路径与你预期的路径进行比较。当智能体达成结果的过程与产出本身同样重要时，可以使用它们。

DeepEval提供四组托管的开源指标。

  1. 任务与目标完成情况包括 TaskCompletion、GoalAccuracy 和 ConversationCompleteness。
  2. 对话质量包括 TurnRelevancy、KnowledgeRetention 和 Summarization。
  3. 工具使用包括 ToolUse。
  4. 安全性包括 Bias、Toxicity 和 PIILeakage。

这些指标对多轮对话智能体尤其有用。ConversationCompleteness 能发现智能体回答了最新消息，却悄悄丢掉了先前请求的情况。KnowledgeRetention 能发现智能体忘记了用户在三轮对话前说过的内容的情况。

AutoEval提供更具针对性的信号。

  1. Security 会标记恶意输出，例如试图注入指令或泄露系统提示词的内容。
  2. Possible 能发现过度谨慎的智能体错误地宣称有效任务无法完成的情况。
  3. Humor 对面向消费者的智能体很重要，因为个性也是产品的一部分。

自定义评估器。当目录中没有合适的评估器时，你可以编写自定义的 LLM 裁判。

每个评估器的精确定义、评分量表和输入要求，都列在 AgentCore 文档的提示词模板库中。其中包括它使用的裁判提示词、运行于追踪记录级还是会话级，以及是否需要参考答案或预期执行轨迹。你可以调用 ListEvaluators API，在一次响应中获取完整目录和你自己的自定义评估器。

多维度评估器

到目前为止介绍的每个评估器，都会为每条追踪记录或每个会话返回一个分数。在衡量单一行为时，这种方式很合适。但在业务结果映射的第 2 步中，每个评估器很少只对应一种行为。客服回复必须解决问题、遵循退款和数据政策，并保持专业。一个同时权衡这三个方面的裁判会返回一个数字，你无法判断是哪项标准决定了这个分数。

多维度评估器是一种自定义 LLM 裁判，使用一组维度来代替单一量表。每个维度都有自己的名称、指令，以及数值型或类别型量表。裁判读取一次追踪记录，并在同一次调用中对所有维度评分。AgentCore 为每个维度返回一个结果。

图 5　多维度评估器通过一次裁判调用对多个维度评分，为每个维度返回一个结果，不生成综合分数

当你的成功标准可能各自独立地出现问题时，可以使用多维度评估器，例如答案准确却不合规，或问题得到解决但措辞粗鲁。它还要求每项标准都能根据同一组证据作出判断，这样一次裁判调用就能替代多个反复读取同一条追踪记录、几乎相同的评估器。对各项标准分别评分后，你就可以逐项设置通过门槛。如果某次发布改善了语气，却降低了政策合规性，就应判定为不通过，而单一的混合分数会掩盖这一点。

当成熟的内置或第三方指标已经覆盖某些标准时，例如 Builtin.Correctness 或 ThirdParty.DeepEval.PIILeakage，应将这些标准保留在独立的评估器中。当标准需要不同的评估层级或裁判模型时，也应分别评估，因为同一个评估器中的各维度共享同一层级和模型。对于需要基准真值的标准，例如 {expected_response} 或 {assertions}，同样应当分开。将无需参考答案的标准放在独立评估器中，可以使其继续用于实时流量。

按智能体类型划分的评估器组合示例

以下每组组合都从最契合业务结果的两三个评估器开始。当你发现初始组合遗漏的失败模式时，再添加其他评估器。标记为“需要基准真值”的评估器只能用于批量评估，因为实时流量没有参考答案或预期路径。

客户支持 多步骤研究 领域内容（医疗、法律、金融）
业务结果 在一次会话中解决问题，且不产生下游风险 通过既定工作流程给出完整、来源充分的答案 在所属领域内给出正确、无偏见且安全的答案
主要风险 遗漏请求，回复不安全或不合规 通过错误的工具调用路径得到正确答案，或在长会话中丢失上下文 错误答案。错误答案比没有答案更糟。
起步选用

Builtin.GoalSuccessRate（核心指标）

ThirdParty.DeepEval.ConversationCompleteness

ThirdParty.DeepEval.PIILeakage

Builtin.TrajectoryAnyOrderMatch（需要基准真值）

ThirdParty.DeepEval.GoalAccuracy

ThirdParty.DeepEval.KnowledgeRetention

Builtin.Correctness（需要基准真值）

ThirdParty.DeepEval.PIILeakage

ThirdParty.AutoEval.Security
按需添加

ThirdParty.DeepEval.Toxicity

ThirdParty.AutoEval.Security（敏感账户数据）

Builtin.Helpfulness

Builtin.SkillInstructionFollowing

ThirdParty.AutoEval.Possible

ThirdParty.DeepEval.Bias

Builtin.Helpfulness
派生评估器 可选 如果推理必须在你的账户内进行，可用于执行轨迹和技能指标 几乎总是需要，以确保每次裁判调用都处于你的数据治理范围内

运行评估的三种模式

AgentCore 支持三种评估模式。

按需评估能提供最快的反馈循环。在开发或调试期间，将会话直接传给 client.evaluate()。系统中的每个评估器，包括第三方评估器，都支持这种模式。

import boto3

client = boto3.client('bedrock-agentcore')

response = client.evaluate(
    evaluatorId="ThirdParty.DeepEval.TaskCompletion",
    evaluationInput={"sessionSpans": session_span_logs}
)

for result in response["evaluationResults"]:
    print(f"Value: {result.get('value')}")
    print(f"Explanation: {result.get('explanation', '')}")

在线评估连接到正在运行的智能体运行时，并按配置的比例对真实流量采样。这是生产环境的健康状况信号。内置评估器和第三方评估器可以在同一份在线评估配置中自由混用。

批量评估针对一组固定会话运行既定的评估器组合，这组会话就是你在发布前进行回归测试的黄金数据集。可以用它来确认，提示词变更或模型升级在你关心的每个维度上都保持了质量。

三种模式使用相同的评估器 ID。从开发阶段的按需测试切换到生产环境的在线评估，只需更改配置，无需重写代码。

整合应用

选择哪些评估器，正日益成为难点。先选出最能体现业务结果是否达成的两三种行为，并优先衡量它们。当你发现现有评估器组合遗漏了某种失败时，再添加评估器。

要查看完整目录，可以调用 ListEvaluators API。它会在一次响应中返回内置、DeepEval 和 AutoEval 评估器，以及你账户中的所有自定义评估器。在选择任何评估器之前，先回答两个问题。“这个智能体取得成功时是什么样子？”以及“追踪记录中的什么行为表明它已经成功？”
